interest: Illuminates Occupation legal reforms, legislative indexes, civil liberties growth, public service strike controversies, and zaibatsu deconcentration policies.
overview: This file documents the fundamental reconstruction of Japan's legal, judicial, and economic structures under the Allied Occupation between 1946 and 1949. It details the abrogation of wartime industrial controls, provisional adjustments to the Code of Criminal Procedure under the new Constitution, and extensive SCAP indexes of Diet-enacted legislation. In addition, the collection traces the development of civil liberties and the Japan Civil Liberties Union, diplomatic and domestic disputes over anti-strike provisions in the National Public Service Law, and policy deliberations concerning zaibatsu deconcentration and antitrust revisions.
